distribution.title: The data will be collected with the purpose to get initial evaluation of green transition in the healthcare sector by the Latvian population. The data will reveal public opinion about respondents` reflection on the reforms in the health care sector that accompany green transition, their experiences with solutions that aim to reduce the GHG emissions in the healthcare sector, their everyday routines in health preservation, their expectations regarding other actors. As the result, the data would help to understand current situation and draw some perspectives of enabling Homo Climaticus.

dataset.description:
With the purpose to examine 4 case studies (hospitals) in Latvia, individual interviews (n=40) will be carried out. Examining experiences of the green transition, hospital administration and employees (including healthcare practitioners) as well as representatives of patients' organizations will be interviewed in order to map the users` knowledge and experience with green reforms introduced in the healthcare sector. These interviews will provide in-depth knowledge on the inequalities that might be brought about or exacerbated by the EGD in the sector. 
In addition, focus group discussions with the involved stakeholders will address the opportunities and limitations of healthcare in the circumstances of green transition, with the aim to sketch a map of inequalities in the healthcare sector, which should be taken into account to enable and empower a Homo Climaticus.

distribution.title:
Data are collected to achieve the objectives and prepare the deliverables of the project, i.e. to map inequalities in the healthcare sector brought about or exacerbated by green transition, and to provide recommendations to overcome them. For this, 4 case studies (hospitals) in Latvia have been proposed, in which individual interviews (n=40) will be carried out. Hospital administrations and employees (including healthcare practitioners) as well as representatives of patients' organizations will be interviewed in order to map the users' knowledge and experience with green reforms introduced in the health care sector. 
In addition, focus group discussions with the involved stakeholders  will address the opportunities and limitations of healthcare in the circumstances of green transition, aiming at providing a map of inequalities in the healthcare sector, which should be taken into account for to enable and empower a Homo Climaticus.

dmp.description:
The project aims to study inequalities created or facilitated by the European Green Deal (EGD) in the healthcare sector, identifying the impact of climate policy on healthcare practitioners and socially vulnerable groups, as well as proposing recommendations for governance solutions to promote a socially responsible green transition.
Through a co-creation design, recommendations to policy makers for ensuring a socially responsible green transition in the healthcare sector will be elaborated, and a road-map for a pilot project for further implementation will be provided. The project is based on a mixed research design. By analysis of scientific literature and documents, and conducting a public opinion survey, semi-structured interviews and focus groups, the research team will identify key inequalities created or facilitated by green transition in the health care, and investigate perceptions and experiences with reforms with primary focus on hospitals. For that, case studies in four hospitals will be carried out. Recommendations for the socially responsible green transition in the healthcare will be developed, involving all stakeholders in the co-creation process.
The Data Management Plan of the project describes the data management life cycle including specific standards of the databases in terms of formats, metadata, sharing, archiving and preservation. The DMP will clarify which data will be open access, and the procedure to gain access to them.
dmp.ethical_issues_description: Conducting of survey involves personal data. However, the survey will be conducted by a market research company selected as a result of the procurement procedure. The survey, using the questions defined by the project's team, will take the form of interviews at the places of residence of the population or by telephone, forming a representative sample (at least 1000 people) corresponding to the latest information of the Office of Citizenship and Immigration Affairs regarding the structure of the population in Latvia. Interviewees will be informed about the research, its objectives and will be asked to give their consent to participate in the survey. They will receive information on the use of their personal data. Personal data will be provided voluntarily. If any of the respondents will not want or will be unable to provide certain data (e.g. answer a question), the survey will include the option of choosing an answer - no answer/difficult to answer. These responses will be included in the survey results.
